name: South Asia pre-monsoon heat
headline: Heat built mid-April after western disturbances ended.
numbers: 47+ (early count): at least 37 in India and 10 in Pakistan; the true toll is probably higher (summary of reports)

sections.The trigger: Heat built mid-April after western disturbances ended.
sections.What amplified it: Above 46 °C in many cities; record power demand.
sections.Climate signal: WWA (14 May 2026): human-induced warming made this April heatwave in Pakistan and northwest India (the 15-day maximum temperature, 15–29 April 2026) about 3 times more likely (central estimate 2.9; 95% interval 0.16 to 242) and about 0.9 °C hotter (95% interval −0.6 to +2.4 °C) than in a pre-industrial climate: central estimates with very wide intervals, not a rise of the average temperature of South Asia.
sections.Still open: Summary entry: the full deep-dive (day-by-day timeline, steering, how it ended, sources) has not been written yet. It will be added as the log works back through the year.
